# Stirling Generators
# Operation
Requires a matching fuel module, room oxygen and MV or HV cable. Emits hot carbon dioxide. Fuel consumption follows the selected target, even when network demand is lower. Loss of oxygen or fuel stops the engine.
# Fuel Modules
Stop the engine and unscrew its service hatch to install a module. Use a crowbar to remove it. Compact and Standard modules fit matching chassis. Fuel and upgrades remain in the removed module.
Close the maintenance panel before adding fuel. Loose modules can be filled directly. There are no separate fuel lids or latches.
Hoppers accept wood, coal, plasma sheets and fuel-grade plasma rods. Hoppers catch thrown compatible fuel; an installed hopper requires a closed maintenance panel. Tanks accept Welding Fuel, Ethanol and Plasma reagent.
Basic hopper capacity: 40 pieces Compact, 120 Standard. At rated output, a full plasma load lasts 2.5 / 3 hours; coal 2 / 2.4 hours; wood 1.25 / 1.5 hours.
Basic tank capacity: 500u Compact, 1500u Standard. Welding Fuel lasts 2.5 / 3 hours at rated output. Ethanol provides 80 percent and Plasma 120 percent of Welding Fuel's endurance.
# Upgrades and Handling
Capacitors raise the output ceiling and ramp rate. Manipulators reduce fuel consumption. Remove a module and use an RPED to upgrade its Matter Bin: R2 / R3 / R4 capacity is 120 / 140 / 160 percent. RPED upgrades do not change intake type.
At 80 percent remaining integrity, liquid tanks leak 2 percent of capacity. Each further 2 percent integrity lost releases another 2 percent of capacity. Large hits count each crossed step. Leaks occur only on damage; repairs cause no leakage. Damage does not spill solid fuel.
